site_description: RCOS is an open-source, shared system for organizing intentional communities. Clear, ready-to-use structures for decision-making, roles, resource sharing, and handling conflicts.
language_switcher_fallback_tooltip: Not yet translated — will show English on this page
home_hero_eyebrow: An open standard for intentional communities
home_hero_lead: Every community runs on rules, but most of them are never written down. Then a crisis forces the question, and the group has to decide in a hurry. RCOS collects those questions up front, so you can answer them calmly and together, before it hurts.
home_story_heading: The day nobody knew the rule
home_story_step1_body: A long-time member moves away. Everyone is sad, and in the middle of that grief a practical question comes up: what happens to their tools? Their room? Their share of the house they helped build? Nobody had ever decided.
home_story_step1_alt: A member walks away down the path with a backpack and bags while the others watch, a wheelbarrow of belongings beside them.
home_story_step2_body: The group decides on the spot, under pressure and full of emotion. It's the best they can do in that moment, but not the choice they would have made with a clear head.
home_story_step2_alt: The group sits in a tense circle: one person holds their head in their hands while others argue.
home_story_step3_body: Some people feel it was unfair. Old tensions come back. What started as grief turns into conflict, and it takes months to settle.
home_story_step3_alt: An argument breaks out: people talk over each other, some with crossed arms, some pointing.
home_story_step4_body: Afterwards, the group sits down and writes a clear rule for next time: what belongs to whom, how leaving works, and who takes over which jobs.
home_story_step4_alt: The group sits on the grass and writes their rules together on a large sheet.
home_story_step5_body: Then someone asks the uncomfortable thing: what else have we never decided? Where is the next crisis we're not ready for?
home_story_step5_alt: One person asks the group a question while the others listen and think.
home_story_punchline: RCOS exists to answer that last question.
home_what_heading: A list of the questions every community has to answer
home_what_body: RCOS, the Regenerative Community Operating System, is an open standard that collects the questions a community should settle before they turn into problems. It doesn't tell you what to answer. Your values, culture and choices stay yours. It makes sure you don't forget to ask.
home_what_example_exit_question: What happens to someone's things when they leave?
home_what_example_purpose_question: Why does this community exist, in one sentence that will still be true in ten years?
home_what_must_note: MUST means every community using RCOS has to give an answer here. The answer itself is up to you.
home_clause_2_1_1: A community MUST define exactly one primary purpose.
home_clause_3_6_2: Exit procedures MUST be explicit, documented, and non-punitive.
home_clause_3_6_5: Asset, role, and responsibility separation MUST be defined prior to exit.
home_layers_heading: Seven layers, from “why we exist” to “how we change”
home_layers_body: The questions are sorted into seven layers. Each layer builds on the ones below it, and a higher layer can never overrule a lower one. That way, a day-to-day rule can't quietly undo your purpose.
home_layers_q0: Why do we exist, and what will we never do?
home_layers_q1: Who belongs, how do people join, and how do they leave?
home_layers_q3: How do money, land, tools and work flow?
home_layers_q4: What happens when things break between people?
home_layers_q5: How does the daily work actually get done?
home_layers_q6: How do we change our own rules without falling apart?
home_parts_heading: Five parts, each with one job
home_parts_body: You don't need all of them at once. Here is what each part is for.
home_parts_core_what: The standard itself: every rule, numbered and sorted into the seven layers.
home_parts_layers_what: Plain-language guides to each of the seven layers.
home_parts_modules_what: Optional add-ons for topics not every community needs.
home_parts_templates_what: Fill-in documents for every part of the core, in several file formats.
home_parts_stress_tests_what: Real situations where communities broke, replayed against RCOS.
home_who_founders_body: Build the structure from day one, instead of patching it after the first crisis.
home_who_existing_body: Find the questions you've never answered before they find you.
home_who_facilitators_body: A shared, neutral language for hard conversations about power, money and conflict.
home_who_builders_body: The whole standard is open and also published as structured data you can build on.

site_library_lead: Everything in the RCOS knowledge base, in one place: the standard, the layer guides, the templates, the stress tests and the tools around them.

site_data_lead: RCOS is also published as structured data, so tools can build on it. Every rule, template section and glossary term, in every language, with a JSON Schema.

hub_library_step1_body: Read the seven layer guides. Together they explain the whole standard in plain language.
hub_library_step2_body: Pick a template, starting with Layer 0, and fill it in with your group.
hub_library_step3_body: Take the self-assessment to find the questions your community has never answered.
hub_layers_lead: RCOS sorts the questions a community has to answer into seven layers, from why it exists to how it changes its own rules. Each layer builds on the ones below it.
hub_layers_step1_body: Layer 0 holds your purpose and the lines you will never cross. Everything above it refers back to it.
hub_layers_step2_body: Each layer has a plain-language guide: what it covers, the questions it asks, and what goes wrong without it.
hub_layers_step3_body: The rules show exactly what the standard asks for. The templates are where you write your answers down.
hub_templates_lead: Each layer asks your community a handful of questions. The templates are where you write the answers down: one document per topic, with the rules it covers, why it matters, and examples from other groups.
hub_templates_step1_body: Your purpose and the lines you won't cross come first. Every later template refers back to them.
hub_templates_step2_body: Each section says what to cover and why it matters, so the conversation stays on track. Write the answers down while you're in the room.
hub_templates_step3_body: Note when the group agreed, keep the document where everyone can find it, and change it only in the way you've agreed to.
hub_stress_tests_lead: Real situations where communities broke, written up as test cases. Each one asks: if this happened to us, would our structure hold, or would we have to improvise?
hub_stress_tests_step1_title: Find the ones close to home
hub_stress_tests_step1_body: Browse by layer below, or take the self-assessment to see which tests match the warning signs you recognize.
hub_stress_tests_step2_body: Read a test as a group. The facilitation guide turns any test into a 60–90 minute session that ends with a concrete next step.
hub_stress_tests_step3_body: If a test shows something you've never decided, it links to the templates where you can write the answer down.
